title: Google Review NFC Tabletop Prompts — Acrylic Stands / Tent Cards / Bill Presenters with NTAG213
summary: Use this page when the review prompt is meant to sit on a table, counter surface or waiting-area stand and the goal is to make it visible enough to drive taps or scans without staff explaining every time. Covers acrylic table-tent stands, bill-presenter inserts, host-stand counter cards and check-presenter NFC tent cards (NTAG213 + QR fallback) for restaurants, cafes, bars, hotel lounges, salon waiting areas and clinic reception desks — operated within FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + Google Business Profile review policy frameworks (no review-gating, no incentivised reviews, 'leave us a review' copy).
heroPoints: Tabletop prompts depend on placement, design clarity and how obvious the action feels without staff help.
Acrylic cards, mini stands and sticker-backed prompts each solve different surface and visibility problems.
The first pilot should test where customers naturally notice and act on the prompt, not just where the team wants it to sit.

brief.label: Tabletop placement form-factor library
items: Acrylic table-tent stand — clear acrylic A-frame with NFC card inserted; restaurant + bar standard.
Acrylic block stand — solid acrylic block with NFC card embedded; salon + spa upmarket finish.
Bill-presenter NFC insert — NFC card slipped into check-presenter for end-of-meal prompt.
Host-stand counter card — vertical NFC card stand at hostess / front-desk position.
Tabletop tent card (printed cardstock with embedded inlay) — disposable tent card for events / pop-ups.
Wood-veneer tent stand — premium FSC bamboo / walnut for boutique / luxury hospitality.
Counter sticker — peel-and-stick NFC + QR sticker on smooth surface (counter / glass / acrylic).
Magnetic backplate version — refrigerator / metal-surface mountable for office / clinic break rooms.

brief.label: Vertical-specific placement strategy
items: Restaurants — table-tent on each table or bill-presenter at end of meal; peak satisfaction = post-dessert / pre-payment.
Cafes + bars — counter-top at register + table-tent at seated areas; peak satisfaction = at-pickup / mid-drink.
Hotel lounges + lobbies — coffee-table tent + concierge-desk counter card; peak satisfaction = check-out morning.
Salons + spas — at-station tent (visible during service) + check-out counter card; peak satisfaction = end-of-service.
Clinics + medical offices — waiting-room side table + appointment-desk counter card; peak satisfaction = post-appointment.
Dental practices — chairside counter card + check-out tent; peak satisfaction = at-checkout.
Auto dealerships + service — service-bay waiting-area tent + check-out counter card.
Veterinary practices — exam-room side table + check-out counter card.

brief.label: Chip + memory + form factor
items: NTAG213 (144 B) — baseline; rewritable URL; 90% of programme volume.
NTAG215 (504 B) — premium variant for cards with vCard + review URL hybrid.
QR fallback — printed alongside NFC for older phones / non-NFC users.
Acrylic 4-mm clear stand — laser-cut, polished edges, 80×120 mm typical insert size.
Wood veneer 6-mm — laser-engraved branding + slot for NFC card insert.
Bill-presenter slot insert — sized to standard 90×54 mm credit-card slot.
Counter card 80×140 mm portrait — vertical with embedded weighted base.
Magnetic backplate option — for break-room / kitchen / office surface mounting.

brief.label: Copy + design framework
items: Headline: 'Loved your visit? Tap here to leave a review' — never 'Leave us 5 stars'.
Brand colours + logo + Google logo + star graphic.
QR code printed below NFC tap zone — ≥15 mm × 15 mm with 4 mm quiet zone (ISO/IEC 18004).
Tap zone marker: 'Tap your phone here' arrow + Apple / Android compatibility note.
Multi-language overlays for international hospitality (EN / FR / ES / DE / ZH / JA).
Avoid pressure language; respect customer choice.
Brand-standard locked: BU customisation gated through brand approval.
Multi-location: per-location encoded URL; centrally controlled design template.

brief.label: FTC + Google compliance framework
items: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 (effective Oct 21, 2024) — rule against fake / AI-generated / insider / paid-positive reviews.
FTC Endorsement Guides — material-connection disclosure for incentivised reviews.
Google Business Profile review policy — no review-gating (only-positive customers asked).
Card copy: 'Leave us a review' — NEVER 'Leave us a 5-star review'.
Cards offered to ALL customers — not selectively to satisfied only.
No incentivisation: no discount + no entry-to-prize-draw + no free item for review.
EU Digital Services Act — review-source transparency obligations for EU operators.
ACCC (AU) + CMA (UK) — equivalent fake-review prohibitions.

brief.label: Programme economics + ROI
items: Per-stand BOM: $5–$15 acrylic stand + NFC card combined; $3–$8 sticker; $15–$40 wood-veneer.
Per-location cost: typically $50–$300 depending on number of stands per location (5–20 stands).
Review-velocity uplift: 30–60% increase via passive tabletop placement (lower than counter-handoff but still meaningful).
Multi-location estate: $5K–$50K initial deployment for 100–1000 location chain.
Reorder cycle: 12–18 months typical; brand-refresh trigger or new-location rollout.
Replacement reserve: 5–10% per year for damaged / lost stands (higher than counter cards due to handling).
Supplementary to counter-handoff: tabletop is a passive layer; combine with active staff-prompt for max conversion.
ROI compared to paid review platforms: 70–80% lower per-review acquisition cost.

brief.label: Operations + lifecycle
items: Daily wipe-down compatible: choose materials that survive cleaning chemistry.
Theft / loss replacement: weighted base + magnetic backplate reduces accidental movement.
Damage-resistance: acrylic survives normal handling; wood-veneer scratches over time.
Multi-location resupply: shipped pre-sorted by location with location-specific URLs encoded.
Off-cycle replacement: damaged stand returned for refurb / chip transfer to new stand.
Brand refresh: 12–18 month design + URL refresh aligned with brand-standard book update.
Per-stand analytics: GBP review velocity per location; harder to attribute to specific table without per-table encoding.
Per-table encoding (advanced): each table gets unique sub-URL for table-level conversion analytics.

brief.label: Implementation programme stages
items: Stage 1 — GBP audit + per-location review-link capture.
Stage 2 — Vertical-specific placement strategy + form factor decision per surface.
Stage 3 — Stand BOM + chip + design + copy lock-in.
Stage 4 — FTC + Google compliance review + brand-standard sign-off.
Stage 5 — Production + per-location encoding + assembly.
Stage 6 — Despatch + on-site staff training + soft-launch one location.
Stage 7 — Full estate rollout + GBP velocity tracking.
Stage 8 — Quarterly placement audit + reorder cycle + analytics review.

before: Single counter card at register; staff hand to customer at checkout.
Customers seated away from counter never see the prompt during peak satisfaction window.
Staff prompt completion rate inconsistent — varies by shift + individual rep.
End-of-meal moment misses prompt entirely; customer leaves without acting.
Attribution: counter cards alone capture 40–70% review velocity uplift baseline.
Single-touch programme — no redundancy if staff prompt fails.
after: Counter card + per-table tent — both placement layers active simultaneously.
Customers see prompt during meal / service at peak satisfaction window.
Passive layer captures customers who never reach counter.
End-of-meal bill-presenter NFC card adds third touchpoint at payment.
Combined uplift: 60–90% review velocity vs verbal-only baseline (additive layers).
Multi-touch programme — redundancy + per-touchpoint conversion attribution.

dataHighlight.heading: Tabletop placement uplift atop counter-card baseline
dataHighlight.text: Tabletop NFC review prompts (acrylic table-tent stands, bill-presenter inserts, host-stand counter cards, wood-veneer tent stands) deliver 30–60 % review-velocity uplift as a passive layer atop active counter-card handoff — combining to drive 60–90 % combined uplift vs verbal-only baselines in restaurants, cafes, hotel lounges, salons + spas, clinics, dental practices, auto-dealership service-bays and veterinary practices. Per-stand BOM ranges $5–$15 acrylic + NFC card combined, $3–$8 sticker, $15–$40 wood-veneer; per-location cost typically $50–$300 for 5–20 stands per location. Compliance framework: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + FTC Endorsement Guides + Google Business Profile review policy + EU Digital Services Act + ACCC + CMA — all enforce no review-gating, no incentivisation, 'leave us a review' (not '5-star review') copy. Tabletop format library spans 8 vertical-specific placements: restaurant table-tent + bill-presenter (peak post-dessert / pre-payment), cafe + bar counter-top + table tent, hotel lounge coffee-table + concierge-desk, salon at-station + check-out counter, clinic waiting-room + appointment-desk, dental chairside + check-out, auto-service-bay waiting-area, vet exam-room + check-out.

items.label: Week 1 — GBP audit + vertical-specific placement plan
items.text: Verify Google Business Profile claimed + verified per location. Generate short review URL per location. Map physical placements per location: counter card + table-tent + bill-presenter + waiting-room tent. Decide passive-only vs hybrid (passive + active staff handoff).

items.label: Week 2 — Stand form factor + chip + design lock-in
items.text: Form factor: acrylic table-tent vs wood-veneer vs bill-presenter slot vs counter sticker. Chip: NTAG213 baseline. Design: brand colours + 'Loved your visit? Tap to leave a review' headline + Google logo + star graphic + QR fallback below NFC zone.

items.label: Week 3 — FTC + Google policy compliance review
items.text: Validate copy: no '5-star' language, no review-gating, no incentivisation. Confirm 'leave us a review' standard. Sign off legal + brand teams. Lock multi-language overlays if international.

items.label: Week 4 — Production + per-location encoding + assembly
items.text: Production wave on confirmed chip + design + form factor. Each NFC card encoded with location-specific GBP URL. Acrylic / wood stand assembled with NFC card insert. Pre-sorted shipping by location.

items.label: Week 5–6 — Despatch + on-site placement + soft-launch
items.text: Distribute to locations. Staff training on placement consistency + cleaning protocol. Soft-launch one location; monitor placement persistence + customer interaction observation.

items.label: Month 2 — Full rollout + per-location GBP velocity tracking
items.text: Full estate rollout. Track per-location review velocity in GBP analytics. Identify high-performing placements vs underperforming. Adjust placement / copy / form factor based on data.

items.label: Month 3–6 — Optimise + reorder + brand refresh
items.text: Quarterly placement audit. Replace damaged / lost stands (5–10% per year baseline). Reorder cycle synced to brand-refresh trigger (12–18 month). Per-location placement standardisation.

items.label: Year 2+ — Operate + scale + cross-vertical learning
items.text: Vertical context spans hospitality, healthcare, salon-spa, fitness, retail and home-services programmes — each estate carries its own placement-pattern library + reorder cycle + FTC compliance audit cadence. Multi-location estate scale-up + per-location placement governance + per-staff prompt KPI integration into manager scorecards + cross-vertical placement-best-practice sharing.

faq.question: What matters most for a tabletop review prompt?
faq.answer: Placement and clarity usually matter most, because the prompt often has to work without staff explanation and must attract attention on its own.

faq.question: Should a tabletop prompt always be a rigid card?
faq.answer: Not always. A rigid card can feel more premium, but a sticker or integrated stand can be better when the surface, cleaning routine or available space changes the practical fit.
